messages.content:
You are the writer of the discussion described below. You write out the discussion that the participants listed below take part in, under the rules and the flow given.

## Setting
Selection of a seed-stage company for a venture fund's next investment. Five partners at an early-stage venture fund review the companies that cleared the final screening round. One company will receive this quarter's seed investment. Participants: Minako, Toshio, Asuka, Servas and Mio. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Reserve accounts and follow-on calls
- Terms of last winter's credit line
- Security review time before first deployment
- Delivery records of two holdings
- Profile of the exits and the write-off
- Account retention through price rises
- Appraisal needs at the last audit
- Independent checks on holdings' reported figures
- Retained recruiters' placement times
- Adviser bench and partner board seats

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Servas, Asuka, Minako, Mio and Toshio. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the candidates | 4 turns | every participant votes; the candidate with the most votes is selected |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied candidates is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

## Participants
Name: Minako
Age: 28
Gender: female
Personality: Minako is very calm and acts calmly in any situation. Even when those around her are emotional, she grasps the facts firmly and responds calmly. As a result, she is often asked for her opinion and often takes on a leadership role. She rarely shows her emotions, but she also has a kind side that she shows to those she trusts. She can be a little stubborn and is strong in her convictions. She is also confident in her physical strength and never neglects her training.
Concern: Money has been leaving this partnership faster than any plan allowed for, and each quarter seems to end with less room than it began with. Before this cheque goes out I want to know what the years after a first round demand of us, and what we can borrow against when they do.

Name: Toshio
Age: 28
Gender: male
Personality: Toshio has a calm and calculating personality and does not often show his emotions. He has a strong will and is the type of person who steadily moves toward his goals. He tends to take a step back from those around him, is not very assertive, and has an air of mystery about him. Occasionally, he observes things with a sharp gaze and has the ability to quickly assess situations. As a result, he is trusted by others as a reliable presence, but he is cautious about getting deeply involved with others. It seems that he has experienced some pain or suffering in his past, but he rarely shows it to others, and those scars may be connected to his cold-hearted side.
Concern: Nearly everything in the last two cohorts arrived late, and never for the reason written in the plan — something outside the team's own hands always sat between the money going in and a first customer switching anything on. I would rather know now which kind of obstacle we are signing ourselves up for.

Name: Asuka
Age: 29
Gender: female
Personality: Asuka has a calm and logical personality, rarely showing her emotions and carefully judging situations. She may seem a little unfriendly at times, but she is very thoughtful and sensitive to her surroundings. She has strong opinions and will assert herself when necessary. She is not very good at socializing, but she is serious about her work and studies.
Concern: The stories we tell about our wins have drifted a long way from what the returns actually came from. I keep wanting to walk back through everything already funded and see which of it kept its customers and which quietly did not.

Name: Servas
Age: 85
Gender: male
Personality: Servas has a very calm and composed personality. Based on the knowledge and experience he has gained over the years, he often gives advice to those around him. He is an excellent listener and can talk openly with anyone. He also occasionally expresses deep philosophical thoughts, and his words inspire many people. He is full of vitality and always gives positive energy to those around him.
Concern: Our own quarter-end has become the worst fortnight of every three months, and much of it goes on numbers nobody here can check independently. Before adding to the book I want a clear view of what a new holding does to the way we close and report.

Name: Mio
Age: 17
Gender: female
Personality: Mio has a cheerful and energetic personality that naturally makes those around her smile. She is curious and loves to try new things. She can be a little clumsy at times, but people tend to laugh it off and forgive her when she makes mistakes. She has strong opinions of her own, but is also able to listen to the opinions of others, making her a well-balanced person.
Concern: Every company we back ends up asking us for people, and lately the asking takes more of the week than the deciding does. I want a straight look at who can actually be found right now and whose time here is left to give.

## Hidden information
The candidates and the full text of every card are listed here. The participants do not know them before the schedule above says so, and nothing from them may appear in the talk before the round in which it is revealed.

Candidates (see the schedule above):
- A: Clinic Scheduler. A company offering appointment and staffing software for independent medical clinics, including reminders, waiting-list handling, and operational reporting for practice owners.
- B: Harvest Sensor. A company developing in-field sensors and an accompanying service that reports soil and canopy conditions to growers on a seasonal subscription basis.
- C: Fabric Loop. A company operating a collection and resale channel for used apparel, running sorting facilities and an online storefront on behalf of participating clothing brands.
- D: Ledger Bridge. A company building software that reconciles payment records between small merchants and their banks, presenting matched and unmatched transactions together in a single dashboard.

Cards (see the schedule above; title: text):
- Reserve accounts and follow-on calls: The fund's reserve accounts show the holdings carrying equipment or stock called follow-on money at twice the modelled rate, and two called it a year early.
- Terms of last winter's credit line: The credit line arranged last winter lends cheaply against stock held for sale, while treating subscription contracts and unbilled invoices as security worth nothing.
- Security review time before first deployment: Deals whose customers hold other people's money or medical records averaged three quarters in security review before a first paid deployment; the rest averaged one.
- Delivery records of two holdings: One holding that assembled its own devices lost five months to a controller shortage, while the tool running inside a partner bank's nightly cycle never missed a release.
- Profile of the exits and the write-off: Both profitable exits sold quiet back-office tooling for financial operations, bought by an incumbent; the single write-off ran its own premises and paid hourly crews.
- Account retention through price rises: The holding serving independent practices kept nine of ten accounts through a price rise, as did the one with instruments in customers' fields; the shopkeeper tool lost a third.
- Appraisal needs at the last audit: Quarter-end marks on anything with a depot or installed hardware need an outside appraisal, which added six weeks and a five-figure fee to the last audit.
- Independent checks on holdings' reported figures: Holdings with instruments in the field, or goods moving across a floor, send readings the partners can verify themselves; the software ones report only their own dashboard figures.
- Retained recruiters' placement times: Recruiters on retainer fill support and rollout roles within weeks, but have never placed a shift supervisor or a seasonal field crew in under four months.
- Adviser bench and partner board seats: Three advisers who ran distribution yards and peak-season logistics joined the bench this year and have taken nothing on, while the partners covering software already hold eleven board seats.

Write the complete transcript of the discussion in the exact Markdown format specified. Output only the transcript.

## Output format
Markdown, exactly this structure; nothing before or after it:

# candidate_selection_0002
## Round 1
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **<Name>**: <utterance, or exactly Skip, or exactly Over>
(one line per participant, in the fixed speaking order; repeat for Turn 2, 3 and 4; a participant who said Over has no line in the later turns of that round)
### Action
- investigate: <Name> -> <card title>; <card title>
(one line per participant; titles exactly as listed)
## Round 2
### Talk
(4 turns as above)
## Round 3
### Talk
(4 turns as above)
### Vote
- <voter name> -> <candidate label>
(one line per participant)
- adopted: <label of the candidate with the most votes>
## Result
- adopted: <label>
